messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: R vignettes and custom CSS
parts:
Hi Richard,

I believe the easiest way would be to just stick all the CSS at the top of your Rmd file (e.g. in a `<style type="text/css">` block).  It's not ideal since it's not in the "head" element of the HTML that way, but it will work.  There's probably something much more clever but haven't played around with it. Anyone know where the Vignette-builder get its html template for Rmd anyway?  It would be cool if that file could be customized (or at least given a custom head element).

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: R vignettes and custom CSS
parts:
I think most web browsers can tolerate CSS in <body></body>, although
you are supposed to write it in <head></head>.

As replied by Carl in another private thread, you can set the option
'markdown.HTML.stylesheet' for the markdown package, which is called
by knitr to compile markdown vignettes, e.g.
options(markdown.HTML.stylesheet = 'your-own.css').

Regards,
